quizzes.stem: A developer asks Claude for a data-import function, pastes it into the codebase and ships it after a glance because it reads cleanly. Which habit did she skip?

options.a: Responsibility: tell the users that an AI assisted with the release
options.b: Delegation: hand the whole function to a different person to write instead
options.c: Description: phrase the request as a longer, more detailed paragraph
options.d: Discernment: execute it against realistic cases and inspect the results

explanation.d: The builder's costly mistake is "Shipping unrun output", and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A builder is someone who owns the whole arc from a customer's problem to a shipped solution", so the function is hers to verify.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the weight for builders falls on "Discernment of code and user experience", and a longer request does not test the result.
explanation.a: Ruled out because telling users is honest but does not test anything, and the natural check is to "Run it, test it, review it".

quizzes.stem: A university student must compose an analytical essay for a graded course that allows AI help only for planning. Which use fits best?

options.a: Ask Claude to probe the outline, then do the analysing personally
options.b: Ask Claude for the full essay, then edit the style to sound personal
options.c: Have Claude write the argument, and cite it as a source
options.d: Paste the essay prompt and submit the response with minor tweaks

explanation.a: A student uses Claude as a partner by questioning the outline while the thinking remains theirs.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "the thinking the course exists to build" must not be handed over, and editing style does not return it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "writing the analysis with Claude and submitting it defeats the point", whatever the citation says.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "submits its essay as their own" is the example of misuse given, and minor tweaks do not change that.

quizzes.stem: A teacher asks Claude for a quiz on a unit and gets ten questions. Which step best reflects discernment and ownership?

options.a: Share it with the class so the pupils can find any faults
options.b: Trust it, because the model wrote a similar quiz last month
options.c: Check the answers and their fit with the stated outcome
options.d: Ask Claude to rate how correct its own questions are

explanation.c: Discernment is judging accuracy and alignment with the stated outcome, and the educator owns what students are taught.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the educator "Checks: accuracy of the content taught", and a past good quiz does not show this one is right.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the educator "Owns: what students are taught, how they are assessed and the fairness of grades", and passing the checking to pupils gives that up.
explanation.d: Ruled out because asking Claude to mark itself is not the check, and the page lists "accuracy of the content taught" among the things the educator checks personally.

quizzes.stem: A non-profit's analyst wants Claude to find trends in a spreadsheet of beneficiaries' names, addresses and health notes. Policy restricts sharing personal data. Which approach is best?

options.a: Upload everything unchanged, since the analysis serves the mission
options.b: Remove identifiers or aggregate first, then analyse and verify
options.c: Upload it and ask Claude to forget the data once the work is done
options.d: Skip the analysis entirely, because personal data can never be analysed

explanation.b: The best answer anonymises or aggregates first and checks results (the non-profit exam angle).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Donor and beneficiary records are sensitive", so the mission does not allow an as-is upload.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rule is "classify first, remove identifiers before analysis", and asking Claude to forget does not remove the exposure.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the course frames data analysis as a normal use handled with care, and the page says "the usual rule applies" rather than a ban.

quizzes.stem: A small shop owner has Claude draft replies to customers about delivery times. One reply promises delivery in two days, a figure the owner never supplied. What is the best response?

options.a: Stop using Claude for customer contact altogether, starting today
options.b: Send it, as the draft sounded confident and professional enough
options.c: Ask Claude whether the figure is right, and send if it agrees
options.d: Check each date and commitment against the actual policy

explanation.d: A reply that states a date is a promise the owner holds, so each date is checked against the actual policy.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the check is "that a confident reply to a customer is not invented", so confidence proves nothing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A small owner has no one else to catch the error", and asking the same tool whether it is right does not check the policy.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "High-volume, low-stakes drafting suits a faster, cheaper model" with a spot check, so stopping altogether is not needed.

quizzes.stem: An illustrator wants to use Claude on a picture-book project and cares about being recognised for her style. Which use fits best?

options.a: Ask it to generate the whole story in her style, then sign it
options.b: Hand it production tasks, and keep the ideas and final choices
options.c: Have it write the narrative and present the result as unaided work
options.d: Let it decide the visual direction, since it knows many styles

explanation.b: Delegate production and keep authorship, the page's guidance for makers.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the maker keeps "the part that makes the work theirs", and a whole story signed by her is not that.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Disclosure matters more here than in many fields", and presenting AI work as unaided is the opposite.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "For a maker the distinctive voice is the product", and the visual direction is part of it.

quizzes.stem: A teacher and a fundraiser each get a draft from Claude. Which pairing of person and essential check is right?

options.a: The first checks the length of the text; the second checks only the layout and the font used
options.b: The first verifies content and fit; the second verifies claimed impact against sources
options.c: The first asks Claude to score its draft; the second trusts it because the mission is good
options.d: The first judges how confident the draft sounds; the second checks how quickly it arrived

explanation.b: The educator checks accuracy and fit with the outcome, and the fundraiser checks impact claims against the source.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page lists "Impact claims and statistics against source" as the check that matters most for a non-profit, not layout.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the fundraiser checks "every claim about impact, every statistic and every funder requirement against the source", so trusting a draft is no check.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the educator "Checks: accuracy of the content taught", and sounding confident proves nothing.

quizzes.stem: A freelancer working for a charity can use a tool that turns the supporter list into personalised letters citing each person's past gifts. Which concern is most serious?

options.a: Those records are sensitive, so identifiers need care before they leave
options.b: The letters might come out a little shorter than the writer usually drafts
options.c: The writer could lose the chance to open each letter differently each time
options.d: Claude cannot produce text in the charity's voice at all, whatever the prompt says

explanation.a: Donor records are sensitive, and the rule is to classify first and remove identifiers.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page names "data analysis with personal records is the classic scenario", not letter length.
explanation.c: Ruled out because greeting variety is not among the risks the page lists, such as "Overstating results to a funder".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the non-profit delegates "first drafts of grant proposals and appeals", so letters in its voice are an ordinary use.

quizzes.stem: Which statement best explains why the same four habits lead to different checks for different people?

options.a: Each person answers for something else, so verification and disclosure vary
options.b: The habits change names depending on the audience of the course in question
options.c: Only builders must check output, since others only draft text for review
options.d: Diligence applies to organisations, while individuals only describe what they want

explanation.a: The page says the habits are shared and that the right answer depends on what the person owns.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The audience courses reuse this frame and change where the weight falls", so the habits keep their names.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the fundraiser's line begins "Checks: every claim about impact, every statistic and every funder requirement against the source", so others check too.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the table row "Diligence is mainly about" gives each column an item, so it applies to individuals too.

quizzes.stem: A bakery owner has Claude draft the ingredient warnings for a new product line from the wholesaler's data sheet. Which step matters most before publishing?

options.a: Ask Claude to rate how sure it is about the whole list of warnings
options.b: Make the wording friendlier in tone for customers who will read it
options.c: Confirm each statement against the original specification
options.d: Add a line saying that an AI drafted the notice, to be fully open

explanation.c: Warnings about ingredients are facts a customer relies on, and the check is against the original specification.
explanation.b: Ruled out because for a small business the check that matters most is "Prices, dates and promises against policy", not tone.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A small owner has no one else to catch the error", and self-rating is not verification.
explanation.d: Ruled out because being open does not verify a claim, and "A customer reply that states a price or a deadline is a promise the business owns".
